scenes.heading: Denormalization
scenes.narration: Denormalization deliberately duplicates data or merges tables to make read queries faster, especially in analytics.

scenes.heading: Why denormalize
bullets: Precomputed and combined data speeds queries
scenes.narration: Denormalization reduces the number of joins a query needs, which speeds up reads. It often precomputes and combines data so queries do less work at run time. This makes it well suited to analytical workloads that scan huge datasets. The trade is that it accepts some deliberate redundancy in exchange for that speed.

scenes.heading: Normalized vs denormalized
scenes.narration: A normalized model avoids redundancy and suits systems with frequent writes, but reading it requires many joins. A denormalized model intentionally repeats data to serve heavy read workloads with few or no joins. Analytics platforms often denormalize precisely because fast reads matter more than compact writes.

scenes.text: Denormalization trades some redundancy for faster reads, which is often the right call for analytics.
scenes.narration: In summary, denormalization accepts controlled redundancy to gain read speed, a trade that frequently pays off in analytical systems.
